name: xhostd
description: Deploy websites, APIs, and services to xhostd from your coding agent. Create apps, push code, deploy previews or production, inspect status, and manage channels, environment, storage, and domains.

interface.longDescription: Use xhostd from ChatGPT or Codex to create apps, write and push code, deploy previews or production to HTTPS URLs, read deploy and runtime logs, and manage channels, environment variables, secrets, database snapshots, and custom domains through an OAuth-authenticated MCP server. It serves developers, and anyone who wants a site or an app online without running a server. Limitations: in a client with no shell, code reaches an app as file commits, with no git push; a secret's value is entered in the xhostd console or uploaded from a shell, never in the chat; and plan changes, payments, member invitations, and git host connections happen in the xhostd console, not through the plugin.
defaultPrompt: Create a one-page site on xhostd and put it online
Show my xhostd apps and their live URLs
Why did my latest xhostd deploy fail?

positive.description: The user asks for the live URL of an existing app.
positive.prompt: List my xhostd apps and give me the live URL of review-site.
positive.expected_behavior: Names review-site and gives its HTTPS hostname, read from the channel object.

positive.description: The user creates a new static site and puts it online.
positive.prompt: Using xhostd, create a static app called hello-review with a one-page site that says Hello, and put it online.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates the app, or reuses hello-review when it already exists from an earlier run. Commits index.html with commit_files, deploys the returned sha, and polls get_logs until the status is success. Returns the URL.

positive.description: The user edits a page of an existing app and redeploys it.
positive.prompt: On xhostd, add a line with today's date under the heading of review-site's home page, and redeploy it.
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the page, adds the date line under the heading with commit_files edits, deploys the commit, and confirms that the deploy succeeded.

positive.description: The user adds a secret to an app without sharing its value in the chat.
positive.prompt: On xhostd, add a secret named API_KEY to review-site.
positive.expected_behavior: Never asks for the value in the chat. Gives the console link with the key filled in, or, in a client with a shell, the upload command that reads the value from a file.

positive.description: The user connects a custom domain to an app.
positive.prompt: On xhostd, connect the domain review-site.lifshitz.io to review-site.
positive.expected_behavior: Attaches the domain to review-site's prod channel; the domain is already attached, so the call changes nothing. Relays the domain's status and DNS records word for word.

negative.description: The request is unrelated to hosting, so the plugin does not trigger.
negative.prompt: Book me a flight to Lisbon next Tuesday.

negative.description: The request is a coding question that needs no hosting, so the plugin does not act.
negative.prompt: Write a Python function that reverses a string.
negative.expected_behavior: No xhostd tool is called. The assistant answers in the chat.

negative.description: The user asks for a plan change and a payment, which the plugin does not make.
negative.prompt: Upgrade my xhostd plan and pay with my card.
negative.expected_behavior: No xhostd tool is called. The assistant says it cannot change plans or take payments, asks for no card details, and shows no plans or purchase link.

publication.release_notes: xhostd 0.75.0 for ChatGPT and Codex: create apps, commit code, deploy to HTTPS URLs, read logs, and manage environment variables, secrets, and custom domains. What changed in 0.75.0: every tool parameter carries a description; the snapshot link tool is now get_snapshot_download_link; email binding left the tools for the HTTP API; the app tools return fewer internal fields; and the tools that delete or restore ask the agent to confirm the target with the user.
